cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, is writing a letter to the believers in Rome. He opens it the way you'd introduce yourself on a phone call to someone who doesn't have your number saved: name first, then what he does. He calls himself 'a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle.'

cards.question: Paul says he's also set apart for the ___ of God.

cards.text: And this good news isn't a last-minute plan. Paul says God promised it beforehand, and it's written down in the Holy Scriptures.

cards.question: Paul says God promised the gospel beforehand in the Holy Scriptures. Who did God promise it through?
Paul says the gospel is about God's Son, who was a descendant of ___ according to the flesh.

cards.text: David, Israel's king, is the Son's family line on the human side. But Paul says that through the Spirit of holiness, He was declared with power to be the Son of God.

cards.question: How does Paul say God's Son was declared with power to be the Son of God?

answers.text: By His resurrection from the dead
By His teaching in the temple

cards.text: Then Paul gives Him His full name: 'Jesus Christ our Lord.' Through Him, Paul says, we received grace and apostleship, and friend, I've never heard a job title that came with grace stapled to the front.

cards.question: Paul says that through Jesus, he received grace and apostleship. What for?

answers.text: To call the Gentiles to obedience from faith
To guard the Law of Moses in Jerusalem
To build a new temple for the church in Rome

cards.question: True or false: Paul tells the believers in Rome that they're also among those called to belong to Jesus Christ.

cards.text: Six verses in, Paul finally says who the letter is for: all in Rome who are called to be saints. That's a LONG intro, and I respect it, because the first time I met a baker, I talked for ten minutes before I remembered to say my name.

cards.question: Paul writes to all in Rome who are ___ by God.

cards.text: With the greeting done, Paul gets going: 'First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you.' Before anything else, he's grateful.

cards.question: Why does Paul thank God for the believers in Rome?

answers.text: Their faith is being proclaimed all over the world
Their church is the largest one in the whole world
They sent money to pay for all his travels

cards.text: Paul says God is his witness that he remembers them constantly, in his prayers at all times. Friend, I can't remember where I put my oven timer, and this man remembers a whole church.

cards.question: In those prayers, what does Paul keep asking God for?

answers.text: That by God's will he may come to them
That Rome's rulers would turn to God
That the church would grow in number

cards.question: Paul says he longs to see them so he can impart some spiritual gift to strengthen them. True or false: he says the encouragement would only go one way, from him to them.

cards.text: Paul wants them to know how often he's planned to come to them. Not once, friend. Not twice. OFTEN.

cards.question: So why hasn't Paul visited the believers in Rome yet?

answers.text: He has been prevented until now
The church asked him to wait
He wanted to finish in Spain first

cards.text: He wants a harvest among them, just like he's had among the other Gentiles. Paul says he's obligated to Greeks and non-Greeks, to the wise and the foolish.

cards.question: That's why Paul says he's so ___ to preach the gospel to them in Rome too.

cards.text: Then Paul says it plain: 'I am not ashamed of the gospel.' Friend, I hide a lopsided cookie at the BOTTOM of the box, and Paul puts the gospel right on top.

cards.question: Why isn't Paul ashamed of the gospel?

answers.text: It is the power of God for salvation
It is popular all over the city of Rome
It is easy for anyone to follow

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the gospel's power for salvation is only for the Jews.

cards.text: Lean in, friend. Paul says the gospel reveals the righteousness of God.

cards.question: Paul says the righteousness of God comes by ___ from start to finish.

cards.text: Then Paul backs it up with Scripture from the prophet Habakkuk (Hab 2:4): 'The righteous will live by faith.' Start to finish, friend, every batch, not just the first one.
